In electrical resistance welding, electrodes must efficiently conduct current (requiring high electrical conductivity to minimize Joule heating at the electrode–workpiece interface), dissipate heat from the weld zone (requiring high thermal conductivity to prevent overheating and degradation), and maintain mechanical integrity under repeated pressure at high temperatures (requiring sufficient strength).  
All three properties are essential for effective performance and longevity of the electrode.  

Final answer: (D)
